<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e`.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9289119221ae3239f0d85e941727e0eefca32b3b` — the merge of head `80b1edc6b4fffc19889c78faa4e86d754906c97e` into base `2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9289119221ae3239f0d85e941727e0eefca32b3b && git checkout 9289119221ae3239f0d85e941727e0eefca32b3b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e 80b1edc6b4fffc19889c78faa4e86d754906c97e && git checkout -B drift-repro 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e && git merge --no-ff 80b1edc6b4fffc19889c78faa4e86d754906c97e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2539ad9860a3e43323fcf35ac80ffee47c8dec3e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f1e07bac7fcd02daf943ced0017058ef292bb3e3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-hook-condition-injected-column-null-guard-at-build.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.flow-null-guards.test.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts` + none in the diff. Read, never reviewed: `packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts`, `packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-publish-batch.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-hooks-and-functions.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-tenancy-guard.ts`. The changeset and `content/docs/automation/{flows,hooks}.mdx` are prose faces, the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the changeset is read here for ② only.

Inputs: card #33435 body and all six comments (claims 6899727412 and 6899772976, scope additions 6884889456, os-dev-report 6900991227, seat ruling 6901005939), the PR body and seven-file list, the net diff `f81e4b6c..f1e07bac`, and the head's check-runs.

Check-runs on the head at review time (65 runs): 25 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 30 still in progress. In progress: `Test Core (1/8)` through `(8/8)`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test UI (1/16)` through `(16/16)`. This verdict does not stand in for any of them. `Test Core (7/8)` had not concluded, so the known `run-date.test.ts` timeout (#34081) is neither seen nor ruled out here; if it ends red, the seat reads its log before it treats the red as that timeout. Completed green and relevant: `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Docs`, `PR-body guards`.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes, read off the tree. All are narrowings; nothing widens.

1. `os build` / `os validate`, record-triggered flow (start `condition`, edge `condition`, `decision` branch `expression`), `record.COLUMN` or `previous.COLUMN` under an ordering or arithmetic operator with no `!= null` guard, COLUMN one of `owner_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `owning_business_unit_id`, `queue`, `organization_id`, where the object as read does not carry COLUMN as a field: accepted before, refused now. Every record trigger (create, update, delete) is covered; the gate keys on `triggerKind === 'record_change'` alone.
2. The same flow slots, the BARE spelling (`owner_id > 'a'`) where the flow's root scope is provable and no variable, screen field or engine name shadows it: accepted before, refused now.
3. `os build` / `os validate`, hook `condition`, any event list, the same six columns: accepted before, refused now.
4. `os build` / `os validate`, hook `condition` whose `events` include `beforeInsert` (alone or mixed with other events), `created_at` / `updated_at` under ordering or arithmetic, where the object does not carry them: accepted before, refused now.
5. NOT named by the PR (S1): `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression`, site `flow_condition` (the MCP `validate_expression` tool). It strips the injected columns and runs the walk with `runtimeWriteType: 'flow'`, so the objects it judges are authored ones and change 1 applies there: it answered clean before and returns the null-guard finding now. That is the answer the publish gate gives, which the tool promises.
6. NOT named by the PR (S1): the runtime publish gate on a `publish-drafts` batch that holds a draft of the flow's or hook's own object. `mergePendingDeclarations` replaces the served object with the draft body, which is stored without the injected columns, so the gate judged that flow or hook over an authored object. Changes 1, 3 and 4 apply there: accepted before, refused now.

Nothing outside the six columns plus the two timestamps is newly refused. The added set is `injectedSystemColumnDefs(obj)` minus the fields the object carries. That function returns `organization_id`, the four audit columns, `owner_id`, `owning_business_unit_id` and `queue`, each gated by `resolveInjectedSystemColumns`, so a tier or an opt-out (`systemFields: false`, `ownership: 'none'`, `tenancy.enabled: false`) that does not inject a column adds no verdict on it. `created_at` / `updated_at` are split off by `PLATFORM_STAMPED_COLUMNS` and reach the gate only through `beforeStamp`. Validation rules, `requiredWhen`, formulas, sharing rules and the object, view, page and `object_extension` doors keep `nullableIndex` (the default of the new `nullable` option; flows and hooks read an empty list under those write types).

An object that DECLARES one of the columns is treated as the author declared it. `injectedColumnsNotCarried` leaves out every name in `fieldEntries(obj)`, so the column stays in `buildNullableFieldIndex` under its own keys: `required: true` or a `defaultValue` is non-null (pinned by the author-declared `owner_id` CONTROL), and a declared column with neither is nullable and refused, as it was at base. A field two packages tie on is carried and gets no verdict, as before.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/spec` minor, title `fix(lint)!`. `Check Changeset` is green. The lint level matches a build-time narrowing under this repo's no-major policy with an ADR-0087 entry; the spec level matches the added migration entry. `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` change no code and need no entry.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: correct. Every change in ① refuses more; none accepts more.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: correct, and for more than the PR says. Changes 5 and 6 narrow runtime readers, which is what the line declares.
- ADR-0087 entry: id `flow-hook-condition-injected-column-null-guard-at-build` matches the changeset marker and is unique in the tree; file prefix `18.` matches the spec major (18.5.0); class `SemanticMigration` with no conversion is right, since whether a null row passes or fails the condition is the author's call. `surface` names the three flow slots, the hook condition, the six columns and the two timestamps at `beforeInsert`, which is the diff. The `reason` overstates one point (S2).
- First-party exposure: the claim is zero hits. A `git grep` at the head for an ordering or arithmetic operator after any of the six columns in `examples/` and package sources finds only the entry's own `replacement` text. Consistent with the claim; `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green.
- The changeset's last paragraph says `Unchanged: the publish gate's verdicts`. The tree moves them in the batch case of change 6 (S1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, `gh api` reads early in the run: reads only. Answered, no action.
- Deviation, the #5017 meta-test PLUMBING list gained `flowHookNullableIndex`, `preStampIndex`, `carried`, `joined`, `into`: forced, since the receiver scan flags any local whose members are read. All five hold Maps or Sets and read no metadata key; the injected columns are read through `injectedSystemColumnDefs` over the tabled `obj`. Answered. The three generic names are a nit (N2).
- Deviation, PR body final as created: answered, no action.
- Open question (`organization_id` exempt at the door, or nullable at both): answered by seat ruling 6901005939, nullable at both. The tree agrees: `resolveSystemInsertOrganization` and the driver's tenant stamp run after the `beforeInsert` chain, and driver-memory stamps no tenant column.
- Out-of-scope, hop leaf through an injected lookup (`record.owner_id.nmae`): judged at neither door; carried by the ruling, the seat files it.
- Out-of-scope, validation rule and `requiredWhen` over an injected column: judged at neither door, pinned by the CONTROL case; carried by the ruling.
- Out-of-scope, `created_at` / `updated_at` residue (flow arithmetic, `previous.created_at`, `beforeFind` / `afterFind` hooks, `external` objects: the door refuses, the build accepts): carried by the ruling.
- Out-of-scope, the message says the object "declares as nullable" a column the author never declared: the door's wording, kept for parity. Noted, not filed (N3).
- Escalated by this review, not in the dev report: the two runtime readers of S1, and the priority question of S2.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`

Agreement with the door, column by column. For the six columns under `record.` and `previous.`, the build now gives the door's verdict at every flow slot and at every hook: the door serves each as a `required: false` field with no default, and the build adds exactly those names for the objects that do not carry them. The guard logic is the unchanged `findUnguardedNullableOperands`, so `!= null` in the same branch and `&&` short-circuit pass, `has()` does not, and a start-condition guard carries to edges and branches, as for a declared nullable field. For the two timestamps at a hook whose events include `beforeInsert`, the build equals the door: there the door's `hookReadsStampedRow` is false, so it keeps every finding, and the build's `preStampIndex` adds both names with no stamped exemption. `afterInsert`, `beforeUpdate`, `afterUpdate` and the delete events add nothing at the build and the door drops the ordering finding, so they agree on ordering. A mixed list (`beforeInsert` with `beforeUpdate`) is judged pre-stamp at both. A flow on update reads the stored row, which can hold null in each of the six, so judging create and update alike is right.

Where the build is still looser than the door: the timestamp residue listed in ③, and a hook or flow on an object the stack does not declare. Where it is stricter: the bare spelling in a flow (N1). Neither is new in kind.

Producers in the live tree against the measured facts. `sys_stamp_audit_insert` (`beforeInsert`, priority 10) writes `created_at` and `updated_at` on every insert and writes `created_by` / `updated_by` only inside `if (session?.userId)`, so a system insert leaves the two user columns empty. The security middleware stamps an empty `owner_id` to the acting user and has none on a system write. `OWNING_BUSINESS_UNIT_FIELD_DEF` says nothing stamps that column yet. `organization_id` is resolved after the hook chain. The hook condition's `record` is made total over the declared fields, so an unstamped column reads `null` and the comparison faults. The docblock's per-column account matches.

S1 (should-fix) — The PR body, the changeset (`Unchanged: the publish gate's verdicts`) and the comment above `flowHookNullableIndex` say no runtime verdict moves. Two do, both read in the code and not run. (a) `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression` at site `flow_condition` hands stripped objects under `runtimeWriteType: 'flow'`, so MCP `validate_expression` now returns the null-guard finding for the six columns. (b) A `publish-drafts` batch carrying a draft of the flow's or hook's object judges over the draft body, which carries no injected column, so the gate now refuses there what it accepted at base (the six columns, and the timestamps at `beforeInsert`). Both move to the card's rule and are inside the declared narrowing, so the level stands. Fix: name both under "What moves" in the changeset and drop the "unchanged" claim for the batch case; pin one case each (a `flow_condition` probe on `record.owner_id > 'a'`, and a gate call with the object in `pending.objects`). The same comment names the extension door, which walks no flow and no hook; say the pending-draft door instead.

S2 (should-fix) — The `beforeInsert` timestamp rule refuses a hook that cannot meet null. Hooks sort ascending by `priority`, the stamp sits at 10, and `HookSchema.priority` defaults to 100, so a `beforeInsert` hook at the default priority, or any priority above 10, runs after the stamp and reads both timestamps set. Only a hook authored below 10 reads null. `hook.priority` is in hand at the lint. The rule equals the door's (#33434), and build-door agreement is what the card asks, so it is not changed here on one side. Two things are owed. In this PR, the entry's `reason` says a `beforeInsert` hook reads `organization_id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` as null "because they are stamped after it"; for the two timestamps that holds only below priority 10, so say "can read … when it runs before the stamp (priority below 10)", as the `hookRunsBeforeStamp` docblock already does. After merge, the seat files a card to make the rule priority-aware at both doors together. For `afterInsert` and `beforeUpdate` the rule is right: the row is stamped or is the prior stored row.

Nits.
- N1 — a flow's bare `owner_id > 'a'` is refused at the build and judged by no door, so the dev report's "build equals door in every cell" holds for the `record.` spelling only. The build treats a declared nullable field the same way, and the new test pins both legs. No change asked.
- N2 — `carried`, `joined` and `into` are excused file-wide by name in PLUMBING; a later local of the same name holding a metadata record would be excused too. More distinctive names would keep the meta-test's reach.
- N3 — the null-guard message says the object "declares as nullable" a column the author did not declare. Door parity; a wording card if the seat wants one.

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-hook-condition-injected-column-null-guard-at-build.ts`: holds against the diff apart from the S2 wording. The replacement and acceptance criteria are executable as written.

`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.flow-null-guards.test.ts`: the seven cases assert `atBuild` equal to `atDoor` per column, per slot, per ownership tier (including a tier that does not carry a column), the mixed event list, the guarded spelling, the author-declared column and the validation-rule control. They do not cover the two readers of S1.

`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts`: the PLUMBING edit is forced and correct (③); N2.

No must-fix.

**VERDICT: PASS** — delta review of `f1e07bac..34790afb` (one commit, 7 files, +108 −19). It closes round 1's S1 and S2 (record 6901107947). No must-fix, no should-fix.

Not run locally. The brief for this round asked for the two pin files and the ablation to be re-run; the container holds no installed dependencies, and a run needs a checkout, an install and a build, which the review's read-only shape rules out. The pins are judged by reading them and by the head's check-runs. The ablation is the author's reading, not mine.

Check-runs on this head (72 runs): 57 success, 12 skipped, 2 failure, 1 in progress at first read (`Check Changeset`, since completed success). The two failures are `Test Core (7/8)` and its roll-up `Test Core`. The shard's log shows one failed test file in the whole job: `@objectstack/scenarios` `test/runner/run-date.test.ts`, three cases, `Test timed out in 5000ms`; turbo reports `Failed: @objectstack/scenarios#test` and nothing else. That is the main-wide timeout of #34081, not this PR. `Test Core (1/8)`–`(6/8)` and `(8/8)` are green, so the lint and metadata-protocol suites, the new pins included, passed in CI.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept set is what round 1 recorded: `validate-expressions.ts` changes three local names and one comment, no logic. The six changes listed in round 1 ① stand, and nothing else is newly refused. An object that declares one of the columns keeps the author's verdict.

The two readers round 1 found unnamed are now named in the changeset's "What moves": MCP `validate_expression` at site `flow_condition` (clean answer to the gate's null-guard finding), and a `publish-drafts` batch carrying a draft of the flow's or hook's own object (published to refused). "Unchanged" is narrowed to the single-item publish gate and a batch that carries no such draft. Both statements match the tree.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still correct: `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/spec` minor, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. `Check Changeset` is green on this head. The new metadata-protocol file is a test and needs no changeset entry.

### ③ Boundary flags

- S1 (round 1): closed. See ④.
- S2 (round 1): closed for this PR. The priority-aware rule at both doors stays a seat follow-up card after merge, as round 1 asked; the PR body says so.
- N2 (round 1): taken. `carried`, `joined`, `into` are now `carriedFieldNames`, `joinedNullable`, `joinedFields`, and the PLUMBING list names the new spellings.
- N1 and N3 (round 1): left as accepted deviations. Agreed; neither affects correctness.
- Seat ruling 6901005939 and the three carried out-of-scope items are unaffected by this delta.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`: renames and a comment only. The comment above `flowHookNullableIndex` no longer names the extension door; it names `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression` and the pending-draft door, which is what the code does. `hookRunsBeforeStamp` and both indexes are byte-identical in behaviour to round 1.

`packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.test.ts`: the new case hands the entry a served object, asserts one finding naming `record.owner_id`, asserts it equals the runtime gate's finding over the same served object, and asserts the guarded spelling is clean. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.injected-column-null-guard.test.ts`: three cases through `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate`. A flow start condition on `owner_id` and a `beforeInsert` hook condition on `created_at` are each refused over the served object, and refused identically with the authored object in `pending.objects`; the guarded flow publishes with the draft in the batch. At base the pending-draft leg returns nothing, so the equality fails there. It pins S1 (b), and the timestamp leg of it.

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.…`: the `reason` now says a `beforeInsert` hook reads `organization_id` as null because it is resolved after the hook chain, and can read the two timestamps as null when it runs before the stamp (priority below 10). That matches `sys_stamp_audit_insert` at priority 10, ascending sort and the default of 100. S2's wording is fixed; the rule is the door's, unchanged, as agreed.

`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts`: the PLUMBING entry follows the rename.

S1 — closed. S2 — closed.

Nit.
- N4 — the PR body's Verification block still carries one sentence from round 1, "the door's verdicts do not move", beside the consumer test counts. The body's "What changes" section and the changeset say the opposite, correctly. Prose only.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
